Sujit Silas · C288 final project
Cleavage siteResults 3D modelsValidation

Targeting MerTK to improve efferocytosis

Efferocytosis is the removal of dying cells by immune cells. I designed proteins to help macrophages use MerTK for uptake and to protect the receptor from ADAM17-mediated cleavage during inflammation. MerTK shedding study

What the models established

Ig1 binder. Restrained repacking improved the modeled fit. Clashes returned when the designs were refolded.

Stalk protector. Low confidence near the cleavage site and inconclusive controls limit what the screen can establish about binding.

The MerTK cleavage region

The reported ADAM17 cleavage bond lies in the membrane-proximal stalk. A binder just upstream could block enzyme access while leaving the Ig domains available to GAS6. MerTK shedding study

    Aim 1 · Design an Ig1 binder

    Bind MerTK at its first immunoglobulin-like domain (Ig1) while preserving access for GAS6, the natural ligand that bridges MerTK to dying cells.

    2. Improved the modeled interface

    3. Tested whether the fit survived refolding

    Aim 2 · Protect MerTK from shedding

    Test whether a binder near Pro490–Ser491 can shield the stalk from ADAM17 and preserve the receptor’s ability to signal.

    2. Screened protector poses

    Prediction scores and geometry

    ipTM estimates interface confidence, pLDDT estimates local structural confidence, and contact PAE estimates positional uncertainty. The Boltz-2 column reports global ipTM. For the initial I32G/W83F case, global ipTM is 0.85 and directional ipTM scores are 0.41 and 0.85. The earlier AF3 nomination rule uses the lower directional score.

    Stalk overlay distances are reported when the local fit RMSD is within and the partner contacts the stalk. Cases outside this rule are labeled as uncertain or off-stalk. Select any row to inspect the model.

    MerTK pathway RNA after burn

    In the burn model, macrophage Mertk and Gas6 estimates were lower, with uncertainty after multiple-testing correction. Adam17 induction was inconclusive. Mmp8 increased in both cell populations.

    Planned experimental validation

    The next experiments test receptor binding, function, and shedding directly.

    Confirm binding and GAS6 compatibility

    Use biolayer interferometry with mammalian-expressed MerTK to measure affinity and GAS6 binding in both addition orders. Prioritize at least twofold affinity over AXL and TYRO3 and at least 80% of the GAS6-only binding signal.

    Aim 1 · Efferocytosis in the mouse burn-wound model

    Confirm mouse MerTK binding before treatment. Compare the lead construct with vehicle and a matched nonbinding control. Quantify apoptotic neutrophils engulfed by wound macrophages and track closure and re-epithelialization. Test receptor dependence under MerTK blockade.

    Aim 2 · Test protection after shedding begins

    Compare wild-type and cleavage-resistant human MerTK at matched surface levels. If cleavage resistance preserves uptake, test an unmasked protector in stimulated macrophages. Measure released MerTK by ELISA, surface MerTK by flow cytometry, and GAS6-induced MerTK phosphorylation.
